source.text: וְאֵ֣לֶּה׀מַלְכֵ֣י הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִכּ֤וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיִּֽרְשׁ֣וּ אֶת־אַרְצָ֔ם בְּעֵ֥בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן מִזְרְחָ֣ה הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ מִנַּ֤חַל אַרְנוֹן֙ עַד־הַ֣ר חֶרְמ֔וֹן וְכָל־הָעֲרָבָ֖ה מִזְרָֽחָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And these [are the] kings of the land whom struck down [the] sons of Israel, and they took possession of their land across the Jordan toward [the] rising of the sun, from [the] wadi of Arnon to Mount Hermon, and all the Arabah eastward:

en.L: Now these [are] the kings of the land whom the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel struck down, and whose land they took possession of across the Jordan toward the rising of the sun, from the wadi of Arnon to Mount Hermon, and all the Arabah eastward:
en.B: These are the kings of the land whom the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} defeated and whose land they took possession of across the Jordan, toward the sunrise, from the Arnon Valley to Mount Hermon, with all the Arabah on the east:
en.R: Here are the kings of the land whom the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} defeated. The Israelites took over their land on the east side of the Jordan River. It reached from the Arnon River in the south to Mount Hermon in the north, and it took in the whole eastern side of the Jordan Valley.

sw.L: Basi hawa [ndio] wafalme wa nchi ambao wana wa Israeli waliwapiga, na nchi yao wakaimiliki ng'ambo ya Yordani upande wa macheo ya jua, kutoka korongo la Arnoni hadi Mlima Hermoni, na Araba yote upande wa mashariki:
sw.B: Hawa ndio wafalme wa nchi ambao Waisraeli waliwashinda na kuimiliki nchi yao ng'ambo ya Yordani, upande wa jua linapochomoza, kuanzia Bonde la Arnoni hadi Mlima Hermoni, pamoja na Araba yote upande wa mashariki:
sw.R: Hawa ndio wafalme wa nchi ambao Waisraeli waliwashinda. Waisraeli walichukua nchi yao upande wa mashariki wa Mto Yordani. Nchi hiyo ilienea kuanzia Mto Arnoni upande wa kusini hadi Mlima Hermoni upande wa kaskazini, na ilijumuisha upande wote wa mashariki wa Bonde la Yordani.

es.L: Y estos [son] los reyes de la tierra a quienes derrotaron los hijos de Israel, y cuya tierra poseyeron al otro lado del Jordán, hacia donde sale el sol, desde el torrente Arnón hasta el monte Hermón, y todo el Arabá al oriente:
es.B: Estos son los reyes de la tierra a quienes derrotaron los israelitas, y cuya tierra tomaron en posesión al otro lado del Jordán, hacia la salida del sol, desde el valle del Arnón hasta el monte Hermón, con todo el Arabá al oriente:
es.R: Estos son los reyes de la tierra a quienes derrotaron los israelitas. Los israelitas se apoderaron de su tierra, al este del río Jordán. Iba desde el río Arnón, en el sur, hasta el monte Hermón, en el norte, y abarcaba todo el lado este del valle del Jordán.

decisions.choice: struck down: defeated in battle
decisions.reason: The verb means to strike or hit, and with kings and armies it means to defeat them in war. The list that follows counts the kings Israel overcame, first those east of the Jordan under Moses (verses 1-6), then those west of it under Joshua (verses 7-24).

decisions.choice: across the Jordan toward the sunrise: the land east of the river
decisions.reason: "Across the Jordan" means the other side of the river. Here the words "toward the rising of the sun" show that the east side is meant; in verse 7 the same phrase is joined to "westward" and means the west side. The direction word, not the phrase itself, settles which bank is in view.

decisions.choice: from the Arnon to Hermon, with the eastern Arabah: the full reach of the land east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: The Arnon is the deep gorge that runs into the Dead Sea from the east and was Moab's northern border (Numbers 21:13). Mount Hermon is the high mountain far to the north. The Arabah is the deep rift valley of the Jordan; "eastward" limits it to the part on the east side of the river (Deuteronomy 3:8, 17).

decisions.choice: the Arnon River in the south ... Mount Hermon in the north ... the Jordan Valley
decisions.reason: Readable adds "in the south" and "in the north" so a reader can picture the span, and calls the Arabah "the Jordan Valley", the part of it in view here, as Deuteronomy 3:17 does.

source.text: סִיחוֹן֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הָאֱמֹרִ֔י הַיּוֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּחֶשְׁבּ֑וֹן מֹשֵׁ֡ל מֵעֲרוֹעֵ֡ר אֲשֶׁר֩ עַל־שְׂפַת־נַ֨חַל אַרְנ֜וֹן וְת֤וֹךְ הַנַּ֨חַל֙ וַחֲצִ֣י הַגִּלְעָ֔ד וְעַד֙ יַבֹּ֣ק הַנַּ֔חַל גְּב֖וּל בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: Sihon king of the Amorite[s], the [one] dwelling in Heshbon, ruling from Aroer, which [is] on [the] edge of [the] wadi of Arnon, and [the] middle of the wadi, and half of the Gilead, and to Jabbok the wadi, [the] border of [the] sons of Ammon,

en.L: Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, ruling from Aroer, which [is] on the edge of the wadi of Arnon, and [from] the middle of the wadi, and half of Gilead, and as far as the wadi Jabbok, the border of the sons of Ammon;
en.B: Sihon king of the Amorites, whose city was Heshbon. His rule reached from Aroer, on the edge of the Arnon Valley, and from the middle of the valley, over half of Gilead as far as the Jabbok River, the border of the Ammonites.
en.R: One was Sihon, king of the Amorites, who lived in the city of Heshbon. He ruled the land from the town of Aroer, at the edge of the Arnon River valley, and from the middle of that valley. His land took in half of Gilead, as far north as the Jabbok River, where the land of the Ammonites began.

sw.L: Sihoni mfalme wa Waamori, aliyekaa Heshboni, akitawala kutoka Aroeri, ulio ukingoni mwa korongo la Arnoni, na katikati ya korongo, na nusu ya Gileadi, hadi korongo la Yaboki, mpaka wa wana wa Amoni;
sw.B: Sihoni mfalme wa Waamori, ambaye mji wake ulikuwa Heshboni. Utawala wake ulienea kutoka Aroeri, ukingoni mwa Bonde la Arnoni, na kutoka katikati ya bonde hilo, juu ya nusu ya Gileadi hadi Mto Yaboki, mpaka wa Waamoni.
sw.R: Mmoja alikuwa Sihoni, mfalme wa Waamori, aliyeishi katika mji wa Heshboni. Alitawala nchi kuanzia mji wa Aroeri, ukingoni mwa bonde la Mto Arnoni, na kuanzia katikati ya bonde hilo. Nchi yake ilijumuisha nusu ya Gileadi, hadi Mto Yaboki upande wa kaskazini, ambapo nchi ya Waamoni ilianzia.

es.L: Sijón, rey de los amorreos, que habitaba en Hesbón, y dominaba desde Aroer, que [está] a la orilla del torrente Arnón, y [desde] el medio del torrente, y la mitad de Galaad, hasta el torrente Jaboc, frontera de los hijos de Amón;
es.B: Sijón, rey de los amorreos, cuya ciudad era Hesbón. Su dominio iba desde Aroer, a la orilla del valle del Arnón, y desde el medio del valle, por la mitad de Galaad, hasta el río Jaboc, frontera de los amonitas.
es.R: Uno era Sijón, rey de los amorreos, que vivía en la ciudad de Hesbón. Gobernaba la tierra desde el pueblo de Aroer, a la orilla del valle del río Arnón, y desde el medio de ese valle. Su tierra abarcaba la mitad de Galaad, hasta el río Jaboc, al norte, donde empezaba la tierra de los amonitas.

decisions.choice: Sihon king of the Amorites, ruling from Heshbon
decisions.reason: Sihon refused to let Israel pass through his land, fought them and was defeated (Numbers 21:21-31; Deuteronomy 2:24-37). Heshbon was his royal city, which he had taken from Moab (Numbers 21:26).

decisions.choice: the middle of the wadi: probably the town that stood in the valley
alternatives: the middle of the stream bed as the boundary
decisions.reason: The words are brief. Joshua 13:9 and 13:16 speak of "the city that is in the middle of the valley" next to Aroer, so this is probably that town; the phrase could also mean the middle of the stream bed, marking the border line. The translation keeps the short wording.

decisions.choice: half of Gilead, as far as the Jabbok, the Ammonite border
decisions.reason: Gilead is the hill country east of the Jordan. The Jabbok cuts across it; Sihon held the half south of it and Og the half to the north (verse 5). The upper course of the Jabbok bends south and marked the western edge of Ammon's land (Deuteronomy 3:16).

decisions.choice: His rule reached ... / One was Sihon ... His land took in
decisions.reason: The Hebrew runs the description on with participles ("dwelling ... ruling"). Balanced starts a new sentence ("His rule reached"); Readable also adds "One was" to tie Sihon to the kings named in verse 1, and "as far north as" to show the direction.

decisions.choice: "Aroeri", "Arnoni", "Gileadi", "Yaboki"; "wana wa Amoni" (L), "Waamoni" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The names of the lands east of the Jordan take the forms already used in Deuteronomy 2-3, so that the two accounts of the same conquest read alike.

decisions.choice: "Sijón", "Aroer", "Arnón", "Jaboc", "Hesbón", "Galaad"
decisions.reason: The names east of the Jordan keep the forms already used in the Spanish of Deuteronomy 1-4, so that the two accounts of the same conquest read alike.

source.text: וְהָעֲרָבָה֩ עַד־יָ֨ם כִּנְר֜וֹת מִזְרָ֗חָה וְ֠עַד יָ֣ם הָעֲרָבָ֤ה יָם־הַמֶּ֨לַח֙ מִזְרָ֔חָה דֶּ֖רֶךְ בֵּ֣ית הַיְשִׁמ֑וֹת וּמִ֨תֵּימָ֔ן תַּ֖חַת אַשְׁדּ֥וֹת הַפִּסְגָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and the Arabah to [the] sea of Chinneroth eastward, and to [the] sea of the Arabah, [the] sea of the salt, eastward, [the] way of Beth-jeshimoth, and from [the] south under [the] slopes of the Pisgah.

en.L: and the Arabah as far as the Sea of Chinneroth eastward, and as far as the sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, eastward, [in the] direction of Beth-jeshimoth, and from the south below the slopes of Pisgah.
en.B: He also ruled the Arabah on the east, from the Sea of Chinneroth down to the Sea of the Arabah, the Dead Sea, in the direction of Beth-jeshimoth, and southward below the slopes of Pisgah.
en.R: He also ruled the eastern side of the Jordan Valley, from Lake Chinneroth, which is the Sea of Galilee, down to the Dead Sea, toward the town of Beth-jeshimoth. In the south his land reached to the foot of Mount Pisgah.

sw.L: na Araba hadi bahari ya Kinerethi upande wa mashariki, na hadi bahari ya Araba, Bahari ya Chumvi, upande wa mashariki, [kuelekea] njia ya Beth-yeshimothi, na kutoka kusini chini ya miteremko ya Pisga.
sw.B: Alitawala pia Araba upande wa mashariki, kutoka Bahari ya Kinerethi hadi Bahari ya Araba, yaani Bahari ya Chumvi, kuelekea Beth-yeshimothi, na upande wa kusini chini ya miteremko ya Pisga.
sw.R: Alitawala pia upande wa mashariki wa Bonde la Yordani, kuanzia Ziwa Kinerethi, yaani Bahari ya Galilaya, hadi Bahari Mfu, kuelekea mji wa Beth-yeshimothi. Upande wa kusini nchi yake ilifika chini ya Mlima Pisga.

es.L: y el Arabá hasta el mar de Quinéret, al oriente, y hasta el mar del Arabá, el mar Salado, al oriente, [en] dirección a Bet-jesimot, y desde el sur, al pie de las laderas del Pisgá.
es.B: Dominaba también el Arabá al oriente, desde el mar de Quinéret hasta el mar del Arabá, el mar Muerto, en dirección a Bet-jesimot, y hacia el sur, al pie de las laderas del Pisgá.
es.R: También gobernaba el lado este del valle del Jordán, desde el lago de Quinéret, que es el mar de Galilea, hasta el mar Muerto, en dirección al pueblo de Bet-jesimot. Por el sur, su tierra llegaba hasta el pie del monte Pisgá.

decisions.choice: the Sea of Chinneroth, the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea
decisions.reason: The Sea of Chinneroth is the lake later called the Sea of Galilee (Numbers 34:11). The Sea of the Arabah and the Salt Sea are two names for the Dead Sea, at the south end of the Jordan valley. The verse traces the eastern side of the valley from the one lake to the other, as Deuteronomy 3:17 does.

decisions.choice: from the south: the direction, not a place name
decisions.reason: The word can be the name of a region of Edom (Teman), but here it names the direction: the southern end of Sihon's land lay below the slopes of Pisgah, the ridge overlooking the Dead Sea from the east (Deuteronomy 3:17; 34:1).

decisions.choice: He also ruled
decisions.reason: The Hebrew simply adds "and the Arabah" to the list of what Sihon ruled in verse 2. Balanced and Readable repeat the verb so the new sentence reads clearly. Readable also gives the familiar names of the two lakes.

decisions.choice: the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the modern name for the Salt Sea, as in 3:16 and 15:2. Literal keeps "Salt Sea".

source.text: וּגְב֗וּל ע֚וֹג מֶ֣לֶךְ הַבָּשָׁ֔ן מִיֶּ֖תֶר הָרְפָאִ֑ים הַיּוֹשֵׁ֥ב בְּעַשְׁתָּר֖וֹת וּבְאֶדְרֶֽעִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] territory of Og king of the Bashan, of [the] remnant of the Rephaim, the [one] dwelling in Ashtaroth and in Edrei,

en.L: And the territory of Og king of Bashan, [one] of the remnant of the Rephaim, who lived at Ashtaroth and at Edrei,
en.B: They also took the territory of Og king of Bashan, one of the last of the Rephaim, who lived at Ashtaroth and Edrei.
en.R: They also took the land of Og, the king of Bashan. He was one of the last of the Rephaim, a people known for their great size. He lived in the towns of Ashtaroth and Edrei.

sw.L: Na eneo la Ogu mfalme wa Bashani, [mmoja] wa mabaki ya Warefai, aliyekaa Ashtarothi na Edrei,
sw.B: Walitwaa pia eneo la Ogu mfalme wa Bashani, mmoja wa Warefai wa mwisho, aliyeishi Ashtarothi na Edrei.
sw.R: Walitwaa pia nchi ya Ogu, mfalme wa Bashani. Alikuwa mmoja wa Warefai wa mwisho, watu waliojulikana kwa kuwa warefu sana. Aliishi katika miji ya Ashtarothi na Edrei.

es.L: Y el territorio de Og, rey de Basán, [uno] de los últimos de los refaítas, que habitaba en Astarot y en Edrei,
es.B: También tomaron el territorio de Og, rey de Basán, uno de los últimos refaítas, que vivía en Astarot y en Edrei.
es.R: También tomaron la tierra de Og, rey de Basán. Era uno de los últimos refaítas, un pueblo conocido por su gran estatura. Vivía en las ciudades de Astarot y Edrei.

decisions.choice: and the territory of Og: a second item after Sihon in the list begun in verse 1
decisions.reason: The verse has no verb of its own. It continues the list of what Israel took east of the Jordan, so "took possession of" from verse 1 is understood.

decisions.choice: of the remnant of the Rephaim: one of the last of an ancient people remembered for their height
decisions.reason: The Rephaim were an early people of the lands east of the Jordan, known for their great size (Deuteronomy 2:10-11, 20-21). Og was the last of them (Deuteronomy 3:11).

decisions.choice: Og, who lived at Ashtaroth and Edrei
decisions.reason: Og was defeated at Edrei after Sihon (Numbers 21:33-35; Deuteronomy 3:1-11). Ashtaroth and Edrei were his royal towns in Bashan, the fertile plateau north of Gilead (13:12; Deuteronomy 1:4).

decisions.choice: They also took
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the verb understood from verse 1. Readable adds a short note on who the Rephaim were, as Deuteronomy 3:11 does.

source.text: וּ֠מֹשֵׁל בְּהַ֨ר חֶרְמ֤וֹן וּבְסַלְכָה֙ וּבְכָל־הַבָּשָׁ֔ן עַד־גְּב֥וּל הַגְּשׁוּרִ֖י וְהַמַּעֲכָתִ֑י וַחֲצִי֙ הַגִּלְעָ֔ד גְּב֖וּל סִיח֥וֹן מֶֽלֶךְ־חֶשְׁבּֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: and ruling over Mount Hermon and over Salecah and over all the Bashan to [the] border of the Geshurite[s] and the Maacathite[s], and half of the Gilead, [the] border of Sihon king of Heshbon.

en.L: and ruling over Mount Hermon and over Salecah and over all Bashan, as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and half of Gilead, [to the] border of Sihon king of Heshbon.
en.B: He ruled over Mount Hermon, Salecah and all of Bashan, up to the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and over half of Gilead, up to the border of Sihon king of Heshbon.
en.R: He ruled over Mount Hermon, the town of Salecah and all of Bashan, as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites. He also ruled the other half of Gilead, up to the border of King Sihon of Heshbon.

sw.L: akitawala juu ya Mlima Hermoni, na juu ya Saleka, na juu ya Bashani yote, hadi mpaka wa Wageshuri na Wamaaka, na nusu ya Gileadi, [hadi] mpaka wa Sihoni mfalme wa Heshboni.
sw.B: Alitawala juu ya Mlima Hermoni, Saleka na Bashani yote, hadi mpaka wa Wageshuri na Wamaaka, na juu ya nusu ya Gileadi, hadi mpaka wa Sihoni mfalme wa Heshboni.
sw.R: Alitawala juu ya Mlima Hermoni, mji wa Saleka na Bashani yote, hadi mpaka wa Wageshuri na Wamaaka. Alitawala pia nusu nyingine ya Gileadi, hadi mpaka wa Mfalme Sihoni wa Heshboni.

es.L: y dominaba sobre el monte Hermón y sobre Salcá y sobre todo Basán, hasta la frontera de los guesuritas y los maacateos, y la mitad de Galaad, [hasta la] frontera de Sijón, rey de Hesbón.
es.B: Dominaba sobre el monte Hermón, Salcá y todo Basán, hasta la frontera de los guesuritas y los maacateos, y sobre la mitad de Galaad, hasta la frontera de Sijón, rey de Hesbón.
es.R: Gobernaba sobre el monte Hermón, el pueblo de Salcá y todo Basán, hasta la frontera de los guesuritas y los maacateos. También gobernaba la otra mitad de Galaad, hasta la frontera del rey Sijón de Hesbón.

decisions.choice: the Geshurites and the Maacathites: small peoples on the north-eastern edge of Bashan
decisions.reason: These two peoples lived beyond Bashan to the north and east. Israel did not drive them out, and they went on living among Israel (13:11, 13; Deuteronomy 3:14).

decisions.choice: half of Gilead, to the border of Sihon: the northern half
decisions.reason: Og held the half of Gilead north of the Jabbok, which met the half held by Sihon (verse 2; Deuteronomy 3:12-13).

decisions.choice: the other half of Gilead
decisions.reason: Readable says "the other half" to make clear that this is not the half of Gilead that Sihon ruled in verse 2.

source.text: מֹשֶׁ֧ה עֶֽבֶד־יְהוָ֛ה וּבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הִכּ֑וּם וַֽ֠יִּתְּנָהּ מֹשֶׁ֨ה עֶֽבֶד־יְהוָ֜ה יְרֻשָּׁ֗ה לָרֻֽאוּבֵנִי֙ וְלַגָּדִ֔י וְלַחֲצִ֖י שֵׁ֥בֶט הַֽמְנַשֶּֽׁה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Moses, [the] slave of Yahweh, and [the] sons of Israel struck them down, and gave it Moses, [the] slave of Yahweh, [as a] possession to the Reubenite[s] and to the Gadite[s] and to [the] half [of the] tribe of the Manasseh.

en.L: Moses the slave of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel struck them down, and Moses the slave of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave it as a possession to the Reubenites and to the Gadites and to the half-tribe of Manasseh.
en.B: Moses the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} defeated them, and Moses the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave their land as a possession to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
en.R: Moses, the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} had defeated these two kings. Then Moses gave their land to the tribes of Reuben and Gad and to half of the tribe of Manasseh to be their own.

sw.L: Musa mtumishi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na wana wa Israeli waliwapiga, na Musa mtumishi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaitoa iwe milki kwa Wareubeni na kwa Wagadi na kwa nusu ya kabila la Manase.
sw.B: Musa mtumishi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na Waisraeli waliwashinda, na Musa mtumishi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawapa Wareubeni, Wagadi na nusu ya kabila la Manase nchi yao iwe milki yao.
sw.R: Musa, mtumishi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, pamoja na Waisraeli walikuwa wamewashinda wafalme hao wawili. Kisha Musa aliyapa makabila ya Reubeni na Gadi, na nusu ya kabila la Manase, nchi yao iwe yao.

es.L: Moisés, siervo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y los hijos de Israel los derrotaron, y Moisés, siervo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, la dio en posesión a los rubenitas y a los gaditas y a la media tribu de Manasés.
es.B: Moisés, siervo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y los israelitas los derrotaron, y Moisés, siervo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, dio su tierra en posesión a los rubenitas, a los gaditas y a la media tribu de Manasés.
es.R: Moisés, el siervo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y los israelitas habían derrotado a estos dos reyes. Luego Moisés dio su tierra a las tribus de Rubén y de Gad, y a la mitad de la tribu de Manasés, para que fuera suya.

decisions.choice: the slave of the LORD: one who belongs wholly to the LORD, a title of honor
decisions.reason: The word is used of a servant who belongs to his master, not one who is hired. Said of Moses (1:1, 13, 15; Deuteronomy 34:5) it marks him as the LORD's own servant, acting with his master's authority.

decisions.choice: gave it as a possession to Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh
decisions.reason: Moses gave the land east of the Jordan to these tribes on condition that their fighting men crossed with the rest of Israel (Numbers 32; Joshua 1:12-15). The gift is described in detail in 13:8-32.

decisions.choice: it: the land of the two kings
decisions.reason: The pronoun is feminine singular and refers to the land, the word used in verse 1.

decisions.choice: slave (Literal), servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: This follows the project's rule for this word. Readable gives the title once and supplies "these two kings" and "their land" so the pronouns are clear.

source.text: וְאֵ֣לֶּה מַלְכֵ֣י הָאָ֡רֶץ אֲשֶׁר֩ הִכָּ֨ה יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל בְּעֵ֤בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן֙ יָ֔מָּה מִבַּ֤עַל גָּד֙ בְּבִקְעַ֣ת הַלְּבָנ֔וֹן וְעַד־הָהָ֥ר הֶחָלָ֖ק הָעֹלֶ֣ה שֵׂעִ֑ירָה וַיִּתְּנָ֨הּ יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ לְשִׁבְטֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל יְרֻשָּׁ֖ה כְּמַחְלְקֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And these [are the] kings of the land whom struck down Joshua and [the] sons of Israel across the Jordan westward, from Baal-gad in [the] valley of the Lebanon and to the mountain the Halak, the [one] going up to Seir; and gave it Joshua to [the] tribes of Israel [as a] possession according to their divisions,

en.L: And these [are] the kings of the land whom Joshua and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel struck down across the Jordan westward, from Baal-gad in the valley of Lebanon to Mount Halak, which goes up toward Seir; and Joshua gave it to the tribes of Israel as a possession according to their divisions,
en.B: These are the kings of the land whom Joshua and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} defeated across the Jordan on the west side, from Baal-gad in the Lebanon Valley up to Mount Halak, the mountain that rises toward Seir. Joshua gave their land to the tribes of Israel as a possession, portion by portion,
en.R: Here are the kings whom Joshua and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} defeated on the west side of the Jordan River. Their land reached from Baal-gad in the Lebanon Valley in the north to Mount Halak, which rises toward the land of Seir in the south. Joshua gave this land to the tribes of Israel to be their own, and he divided it among them.

sw.L: Na hawa [ndio] wafalme wa nchi ambao Yoshua na wana wa Israeli waliwapiga ng'ambo ya Yordani upande wa magharibi, kutoka Baal-gadi katika bonde la Lebanoni hadi mlima Halaki, unaopanda kuelekea Seiri; na Yoshua akaitoa kwa makabila ya Israeli iwe milki sawasawa na migawanyo yao,
sw.B: Hawa ndio wafalme wa nchi ambao Yoshua na Waisraeli waliwashinda ng'ambo ya Yordani upande wa magharibi, kuanzia Baal-gadi katika Bonde la Lebanoni hadi Mlima Halaki, mlima unaopanda kuelekea Seiri. Yoshua aliyapa makabila ya Israeli nchi yao iwe milki yao, sehemu kwa sehemu,
sw.R: Hawa ndio wafalme ambao Yoshua na Waisraeli waliwashinda upande wa magharibi wa Mto Yordani. Nchi yao ilienea kuanzia Baal-gadi katika Bonde la Lebanoni upande wa kaskazini hadi Mlima Halaki, unaopanda kuelekea nchi ya Seiri upande wa kusini. Yoshua aliyapa makabila ya Israeli nchi hii iwe yao, akaigawa kati yao.

es.L: Y estos [son] los reyes de la tierra a quienes derrotaron Josué y los hijos de Israel al otro lado del Jordán, al occidente, desde Baal-gad en el valle del Líbano hasta el monte Halac, que sube hacia Seír; y Josué la dio a las tribus de Israel en posesión, conforme a sus divisiones,
es.B: Estos son los reyes de la tierra a quienes Josué y los israelitas derrotaron al otro lado del Jordán, en el lado occidental, desde Baal-gad en el valle del Líbano hasta el monte Halac, el monte que se eleva hacia Seír. Josué dio su tierra a las tribus de Israel en posesión, porción por porción,
es.R: Estos son los reyes a quienes Josué y los israelitas derrotaron al oeste del río Jordán. Su tierra iba desde Baal-gad, en el valle del Líbano, en el norte, hasta el monte Halac, que se eleva hacia la tierra de Seír, en el sur. Josué dio esta tierra a las tribus de Israel para que fuera suya, y la repartió entre ellas.

decisions.choice: across the Jordan westward: the land west of the river
decisions.reason: The same phrase that meant the east side in verse 1 here has "westward" with it, so the land of Canaan proper is meant, where Israel now was.

decisions.choice: from Baal-gad to Mount Halak: the northern and southern limits of Joshua's conquests
decisions.reason: The same limits are given in 11:17. Baal-gad lay in the valley below Mount Hermon, in the far north. Mount Halak, "the bare mountain", rose toward Seir, the hill country of Edom, in the far south.

decisions.choice: divisions: the portions allotted to each tribe
decisions.reason: The word means a share or division. It points ahead to the dividing of the land among the tribes in chapters 13-21 (11:23; 18:10).

decisions.choice: in the north ... in the south
decisions.reason: Readable adds the directions so a reader can picture the span of the land.

source.text: בָּהָ֣ר וּבַשְּׁפֵלָ֗ה וּבָֽעֲרָבָה֙ וּבָ֣אֲשֵׁד֔וֹת וּבַמִּדְבָּ֖ר וּבַנֶּ֑גֶב הַֽחִתִּי֙ הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י וְהַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ הַפְּרִזִּ֔י הַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִֽי׃פ

records.literal_gloss: in the hill country and in the Shephelah and in the Arabah and in the slopes and in the wilderness and in the Negev, the Hittite[s], the Amorite[s] and the Canaanite[s], the Perizzite[s], the Hivite[s] and the Jebusite[s].

en.L: in the hill country and in the Shephelah and in the Arabah and on the slopes and in the wilderness and in the Negev, the Hittites, the Amorites and the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites.
en.B: in the hill country and the foothills, in the Arabah and on the slopes, in the wilderness and in the Negev, the land of the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites.
en.R: This land was in the hill country, the low hills in the west, the Jordan Valley, the hillsides, the desert, and the dry country in the south. It was the land where the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites lived.

sw.L: katika nchi ya milima, na katika Shefela, na katika Araba, na katika materemko, na katika nyika, na katika Negebu, Wahiti, Waamori na Wakanaani, Waperizi, Wahivi na Wayebusi.
sw.B: katika nchi ya milima na vilima vya chini, katika Araba na materemko, nyikani na katika Negebu, nchi ya Wahiti, Waamori, Wakanaani, Waperizi, Wahivi na Wayebusi.
sw.R: Nchi hiyo ilikuwa katika vilima, vilima vya chini upande wa magharibi, Bonde la Yordani, materemko ya milima, jangwa, na nchi kavu ya kusini. Ilikuwa nchi waliyoishi Wahiti, Waamori, Wakanaani, Waperizi, Wahivi na Wayebusi.

es.L: en la región montañosa y en la Sefelá y en el Arabá y en las laderas y en el desierto y en el Néguev, el hitita, el amorreo y el cananeo, el ferezeo, el heveo y el jebuseo.
es.B: en la región montañosa y en las estribaciones, en el Arabá y en las laderas, en el desierto y en el Néguev, la tierra de los hititas, los amorreos, los cananeos, los ferezeos, los heveos y los jebuseos.
es.R: Esta tierra estaba en la región montañosa, en las colinas bajas del oeste, en el valle del Jordán, en las laderas, en el desierto y en la tierra seca del sur. Era la tierra donde vivían los hititas, amorreos, cananeos, ferezeos, heveos y jebuseos.

decisions.choice: hill country, Shephelah, Arabah, slopes, wilderness, Negev: the regions of the land west of the Jordan
decisions.reason: The central hill country; the Shephelah, the low hills between the hills and the coastal plain; the Arabah, the Jordan valley; the slopes that fall from the hills to the valleys; the wilderness of Judah; and the Negev, the dry south (10:40; 11:16; Deuteronomy 1:7).

decisions.choice: Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, Jebusites: the peoples of the land
decisions.reason: This is the usual list of the nations of Canaan (9:1; 11:3; Exodus 3:8). Here it names the land by the peoples who lived in it, without a verb.

decisions.choice: the land of the Hittites ... / It was the land where ... lived
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "the land of" so the peoples' names read as a description of the land. Readable also describes the Shephelah, the Arabah and the Negev instead of naming them, as Deuteronomy 1:7 does.

decisions.choice: one: a tally, counting each king in turn
decisions.reason: Each line of the list ends with "one", like an entry in a count, and the total is given at the end (verse 24). The repeated word is kept at every level so the list keeps its form.

decisions.choice: Jericho and Ai, near Bethel: the first two cities taken
decisions.reason: Jericho fell in chapter 6 and Ai in chapter 8; Ai lay close to Bethel, east of it (7:2; 8:9).

decisions.choice: the king of X, one;
decisions.reason: The list keeps the Hebrew formula at every level, with a semicolon after each entry, so the count can be followed to its total in verse 24. Balanced and Readable say "which is near Bethel" for Literal's "beside".

decisions.choice: "mfalme wa X, mmoja;" for each entry
decisions.reason: The list keeps the Hebrew pattern, a king and the count "one", so the reader can count the thirty-one kings of verse 24. Every name is kept, in the forms used earlier in the book: "Horma" as in Numbers and Deuteronomy; "Goyimu" as in Genesis 14; the others with the final vowel Swahili writes.

decisions.choice: "el rey de X, uno;"
decisions.reason: As in the English, every level keeps the Hebrew tally, one king at a time with a semicolon after each, so that the count can be followed to its total in verse 24. The town names keep the forms used in chapters 6-11.

decisions.choice: Lasharon: read as a town name, though it may mean "of the Sharon"
alternatives: the king of Aphek in the Sharon
decisions.reason: The word is the name Sharon with a small word meaning "of" or "belonging to" joined to it. It may be the name of a town, Lasharon, or it may mean "the king of the Sharon", the coastal plain where Aphek stood, so that the two entries describe one king of Aphek in the Sharon. The ancient Greek translation reads it in this second way. The translation keeps the name as a separate entry, since the count of thirty-one in verse 24 needs it.

decisions.reason: Kings of Shimron and Achshaph were among those Jabin summoned (11:1). Shimron-meron is probably the same Shimron under a fuller name.

decisions.reason: Neither is named in the battle accounts, and their people were not driven out for a long time (17:11-12; Judges 1:27).

decisions.choice: Kedesh, and Jokneam in Carmel
decisions.reason: Kedesh was a town in the hills of Galilee (19:37; 20:7). Jokneam lay at the foot of Mount Carmel, near the coast; "in Carmel" places it by the mountain (19:11).

decisions.choice: Dor in Naphath-dor: the coastal town of Dor and its district
decisions.reason: Dor was a harbor town south of Mount Carmel. Naphath-dor, perhaps "the heights of Dor", is the district around it, named among the northern allies in 11:2.

decisions.choice: Goiim in Gilgal, as the Hebrew text has it
alternatives: the king of Goiim in Galilee
decisions.reason: Goiim means "nations" and is used as a name, as in "Tidal king of Goiim" (Genesis 14:1). This Gilgal is probably not Israel's camp near Jericho (4:19), since the king is listed among the northern ones. The ancient Greek translation has "Galilee" in place of Gilgal, which would fit the north; the Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: Tirzah: a town of the central hills
decisions.reason: Tirzah is not named in the battle accounts. It later became a royal city of the northern kingdom (1 Kings 14:17; 15:33).

decisions.choice: thirty-one kings in all: a count of kings defeated, not of towns fully held
decisions.reason: The total sums the tally of "one" in verses 9-24. Defeating a town's king did not always mean Israel held the town: Jerusalem and Gezer stayed in Canaanite hands (15:63; 16:10), and much land was still left to take (13:1).

decisions.choice: Thirty-one kings in all
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "all kings, thirty-one". Balanced and Readable put the number first, as a total is usually given.
